summary.one_liner: Flue is a small Python bridge that lets coding agents such as Claude Code run scripts inside desktop applications (Photoshop, Blender, Unity, Office, and others) through each app's own scripting runtime.
summary.what_it_does: Flue installs as a skill for agentic coding harnesses and exposes a bridge command that takes a script from the agent, runs it inside the target application's automation runtime, and returns the result as JSON. The README lists support for Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, Premiere Pro, After Effects and Audition, Blender, Unity, SideFX Houdini, Autodesk 3ds Max, Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint, and Figma (desktop app plus a one-time plugin import). It names Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cline and several other agent harnesses as compatible. The author positions it as an alternative to MCP servers and screenshot-based computer use, since it relies on existing native interfaces (COM, AppleScript, or a local endpoint) rather than defined schemas or servers. Setup is done with pip install flue followed by flue setup, which detects installed harnesses. Documentation is split into human-facing setup pages and agent-facing adapter and contract pages.
use_cases: automate repetitive Photoshop or Illustrator edits from a coding agent
script Blender or Unity tasks from the shell
let an agent make changes in Word, Excel or PowerPoint
drive Premiere Pro or After Effects through scripts
control InDesign layouts programmatically via its scripting API
replace MCP servers for desktop app control
stack: Adobe, Autodesk, Microsoft Office, Blender, Unity and Figma scripting runtimes
notable: Uses each application's built-in scripting interface instead of defining MCP-style schemas or servers
Single pip install with a setup command that registers the skill with detected agent harnesses
Covers 13 named desktop applications across Adobe, Autodesk, Microsoft, game engines and Figma
Returns results from the app as JSON to the agent shell
caveats: Some apps need app-specific setup, which the README says agents should flag to the user
Figma requires a one-time plugin import
The README says the approach is less fragile with the right harness and model, implying results depend on those choices
